description: we are from vancouver and are doing this hackathon for fun!
summary: We developed a website that allows the user to pick certain values on a sliding scale from 1-100 that relate to some key characteristics that must be considered when picking landing sites or locations in general. Namely, these are elevation, terrain roughness, temperature, and water availability. The user can select relative high or low values for these qualities. Then, an algorithm will assess the given values and sort through a dictionary of locations that we found and match the most alike location with the values. It will pick one location for Earth, the Moon, and Mars, and also display the accuracy of the calculation. The results page also provides the elevation and temperature in that location as well as an image of the location. This addresses the challenge since it provides analogous locations among the three celestial bodies while also identifying their key characteristics that need to be considered. It is important since it is an easy to use interface- everyday individuals can also look at it to find similarities and see how locations on Earth can represent the environment on Mars and the Moon.
details: This project takes in user input from a slider which will select values for elevation, temperature, roughness, and water availability. It then uses the combined difference formula to sort through a dictionary of stored locations that have values for the four characteristics and find the most similar one for Earth, the Moon, and Mars. The scale of 1-100 used is a relative scale used for ease of comparison- we looked through the scientific values and sorted them on this scale. The impact of this project is to allow people to find analogous locations among the three bodies with certain characteristics that are important to consider. This was created with HTML, styled in CSS, and has logic implemented in JavaScript. It is then hosted on GitHub Pages. This project is creative since it turns scientific data which is scattered among multiple different data bases into one interactive and visually appealing website that allows for users to clearly see the similarities between Earth, Mars, and the Moon. Furthermore, the algorithm is able to show how accurate the comparison actually is which is another interesting aspect. When making this site, my partner and I had to consider what specific characteristics may be more important, how many locations to use, and how we can look through databases to find the largest variety of values for the characteristics on each of the celestial bodies. Through teamwork and discussion we were able to narrow these questions down into answers and create the final product that is astroAlign.
